<Picture 1> is an aerial photograph used ONLY as a geometric route specification. The red line on it is the camera path through a broad tree-lined residential avenue in Milan: red-tile-roof apartment blocks on the LEFT, a dense avenue tree line and parked cars on the RIGHT, side streets with zebra crossings joining at intervals, a circular piazza with a central fountain opening to the RIGHT midway, and further north wide park lawns on the RIGHT beyond the trees, bright summer daylight. Infer plausible 3D surroundings from the street layout. NEVER reproduce the aerial viewpoint of the picture itself, and under no circumstance let the picture's flat graphics appear in the world.

FIRST-PERSON BICYCLE CAMERA, non-negotiable: camera on the bicycle's handlebar at exactly 1.6 meters above the ground, looking straight ahead horizontally; handlebar grips and both of the rider's hands are ALWAYS VISIBLE at the bottom edge of the frame; the ground fills the lower half; the horizon stays near the middle. The camera NEVER rises above 1.6 m. Absolutely NO aerial view, NO drone shot, NO bird's-eye view.

ONE CONTINUOUS RIDE, no stopping anywhere (total 10.0 seconds, 24 fps):
- 0.0s-3.0s: the ride starts exactly at the southern junction, rolling NORTH onto the avenue over its zebra crossing at steady cycling speed; the wide asphalt stretches ahead, red-roof apartment blocks on the LEFT, a dense tree line with parked cars on the RIGHT.
- 3.0s-6.5s: settle into the middle of the avenue at cruise speed; balconies and shutters of the apartment blocks flick past on the LEFT; sunlight dapples through the tree canopy on the RIGHT; a side street mouth slides by.
- 6.5s-10.0s: keep riding straight north along the same avenue; the circular piazza with its central fountain begins to open up ahead-RIGHT beyond the tree line. The clip CUTS while still moving at full cruise speed — do NOT slow down, do NOT arrive anywhere.
The entire ride must read as one unbroken northbound push up the same avenue.
